name: NestJs
scope: A person with INTERMEDIATE proficiency level in NestJs as a competency should be able to structure applications using modules, controllers, and providers, leverage TypeScript features and Nest CLI, and understand the Nest bootstrap process. They can design modular architectures, avoid circular dependencies, use dependency injection (constructor-based, custom tokens, provider scopes), and manage provider lifecycles. They implement RESTful controllers with proper routing, DTOs, validation (class-validator, pipes), error handling (HttpException, filters), and serialization (class-transformer, interceptors). They integrate with at least one persistence layer (TypeORM, Prisma, Mongoose), handle repositories, transactions, and configuration management (@nestjs/config, env files, ConfigService), and manage secrets and environment-specific settings. They implement authentication and authorization (Passport, JWT, guards, RBAC), basic security (CORS, Helmet, rate limiting), and mitigate common vulnerabilities. They use and create custom pipes, guards, interceptors, filters, and middleware for cross-cutting concerns, and integrate async operations (async/await, @nestjs/bull, @nestjs/schedule, EventEmitterModule) and messaging (Nest microservices, TCP/Redis/RMQ/NATS/Kafka). They design and document REST, GraphQL (@nestjs/graphql), and WebSocket APIs, handle versioning, and combine API styles as needed. They write unit, integration, and E2E tests (Jest, Supertest), manage test environments, and ensure code quality. They implement logging (Nest Logger, Pino/Winston), caching (CacheModule), health checks (@nestjs/terminus), and basic observability (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry). They use Nest CLI, configure TypeScript, linting, formatting, local dev tooling (Docker, nodemon), and debug tools, automate developer tasks, and manage local environments. They prepare applications for deployment (Docker, CI/CD, process managers), handle configuration/secrets in production, ensure graceful shutdown, and troubleshoot using logs and metrics. They collaborate on code reviews, documentation (Swagger/OpenAPI, GraphQL docs), maintain architectural standards, mentor juniors, and coordinate with other teams using agile tools.

{"sections":[{"name":"Core NestJS Fundamentals","scope_included":"- Understands NestJS philosophy (opinionated, modular, convention-driven, DI-centric) and can explain why to use Nest over bare Express/Fastify
- Structures applications around modules, controllers, and providers as the primary building blocks
- Uses TypeScript features effectively (interfaces, types, generics, decorators, async/await) in the context of Nest
- Understands how Nest abstracts over HTTP platforms (Express/Fastify) and what is platform-specific vs framework-agnostic
- Uses the Nest CLI to generate, organize, and maintain application structure (modules, controllers, providers, guards, pipes, etc.)
- Understands application bootstrap process (NestFactory, create, configure, listen) and global configuration (global pipes, filters, guards, interceptors, prefix)
- Knows the difference between synchronous and asynchronous providers/operations and how Nest handles async flows","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Application Architecture & Module Design","scope_included":"- Breaks the codebase into cohesive feature modules, shared modules, and core/infrastructure modules with clear boundaries
- Designs modules to avoid circular dependencies, using forwardRef and refactoring when needed
- Differentiates between global modules and regular modules and uses global modules sparingly and intentionally
- Structures domain logic in services/providers rather than controllers, keeping controllers thin
- Applies layering concepts (presentation, application/service, domain, persistence) within Nest modules
- Organizes internal module structure (controllers, services, repositories, DTOs, entities/schemas, mappers) consistently across the codebase
- Uses barrel files or explicit imports appropriately for maintainable module boundaries
- Understands how to share common functionality via shared modules (e.g., logging, configuration, utilities, base services) without over-coupling
- Designs module APIs (what is exported vs kept internal) based on clear encapsulation principles
- Plans for growth of the application by designing modules that can later be split into microservices if needed","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Controllers, Routing & Request Handling","scope_included":"- Defines RESTful controllers with appropriate routing decorators (@Controller, @Get, @Post, @Put, @Patch, @Delete, @Param, @Query, @Body, @Headers, @Req/@Res)
- Designs clear, consistent, and semantically correct route structures and HTTP method usage
- Uses route parameters, query parameters, and body payloads correctly and validates them via DTOs and pipes
- Applies versioning strategies using Nest's API versioning (URI, header, media type) when required
- Handles streaming responses and file downloads in controllers when necessary
- Knows when and how to use the underlying platform response object (@Res) vs returning values directly from controllers
- Implements content negotiation and returns appropriate HTTP status codes using Nest's conventions and @HttpCode where needed
- Uses route guards, interceptors, and pipes at controller/route levels to keep controllers focused on orchestration
- Separates public vs protected routes logically within controllers or modules","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Providers, Dependency Injection & Lifecycle","scope_included":"- Defines services, repositories, and other injectable providers using @Injectable and understands provider registration in modules
- Uses Nest's dependency injection system confidently, including constructor-based injection and the @Inject token when necessary
- Understands provider scopes (default singleton, request-scoped, transient) and selects scopes based on use cases and performance implications
- Creates custom provider tokens (string, symbol, class) to decouple implementations from interfaces/contracts
- Uses useClass, useFactory, useValue, and useExisting provider configurations to adapt to different runtime needs
- Understands Nest lifecycle hooks (OnModuleInit, OnModuleDestroy, BeforeApplicationShutdown, etc.) and applies them for resource initialization and cleanup
- Manages long-lived resources (DB connections, external API clients, message brokers) via providers with proper lifecycle control
- Uses dependency inversion to decouple services from specific libraries (e.g., abstracting over ORM, HTTP client, cache implementation)
- Avoids service locator anti-patterns and overuse of global state by leveraging DI correctly","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Data Access & Persistence Integration","scope_included":"- Integrates at least one major persistence technology with Nest (TypeORM, Prisma, Mongoose, Sequelize, or similar) using Nest-specific packages or custom providers
- Designs entities/schemas/models and maps them to DTOs, avoiding leaking persistence models directly into controllers
- Uses repositories or data access services to encapsulate queries and persistence logic
- Handles database connections and connection options through configuration and DI rather than hardcoding
- Implements common CRUD operations, pagination, filtering, and sorting with the chosen data layer
- Uses migrations or schema evolution tools (if supported by the chosen stack) as part of regular workflow
- Manages transactions where applicable (TypeORM QueryRunner, Prisma transaction APIs, database-native transactions) for multi-step operations
- Handles common persistence concerns such as soft deletes, optimistic locking, or versioning when relevant
- Deals with database-related errors (unique constraint, foreign key violations, timeouts) and converts them into meaningful HTTP errors
- Implements indexing and basic query optimization awareness from the application layer perspective","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"DTOs, Validation, Serialization & Error Handling","scope_included":"- Defines DTO classes to represent request/response contracts and separates them from internal domain models
- Uses class-validator and class-transformer effectively via Nest's ValidationPipe and transformation options
- Configures global validation (whitelist, forbidNonWhitelisted, transform) to enforce strict payload handling
- Implements custom validation decorators or constraints when built-in validators are insufficient
- Uses serialization features (ClassSerializerInterceptor, @Expose, @Exclude, groups, transformation options) to control API output
- Distinguishes between internal error types and external HTTP-facing error responses
- Uses HttpException and derived exceptions (BadRequestException, NotFoundException, UnauthorizedException, etc.) consistently
- Creates custom exception classes and/or exception filters for cross-cutting error handling concerns
- Configures global exception filters where appropriate, while still using fine-grained controller-level filters when needed
- Ensures that sensitive information is not leaked via error messages or stack traces in production
- Returns standardized error responses (shape, codes) and documents them via OpenAPI/Swagger or other API documentation mechanisms","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Configuration Management, Environments & Secrets (Core)","scope_included":"- Uses @nestjs/config or equivalent configuration mechanisms to manage environment-specific settings
- Loads configuration from environment variables, .env files, and/or configuration files safely and predictably
- Validates configuration at startup (e.g., using Joi or class-validator with ConfigModule) to fail fast on misconfigurations
- Organizes configuration into logical namespaces (database, cache, auth, messaging, external services) and exposes typed configuration accessors
- Avoids hardcoding secrets or environment-specific values in code or version control
- Differentiates between development, staging, and production configuration behaviors (logging, debugging, CORS, security, caching)
- Manages feature flags or toggles at configuration level when needed
- Understands how to inject configuration into providers, controllers, and modules using ConfigService or equivalent abstractions
- Handles dynamic module registration that depends on configuration (e.g., for database, cache, or message broker modules)","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Authentication, Authorization & Security","scope_included":"- Implements authentication using Nest's Passport integration (strategies such as JWT, local, OAuth2, or session-based) as needed
- Configures JWT authentication (signing, verification, expiration, refresh tokens) and integrates it with guards and strategies
- Uses Guards (@UseGuards, AuthGuard, custom CanActivate implementations) to protect routes and modules
- Implements role-based access control (RBAC) or permission-based authorization using custom decorators and guards
- Manages user identity information injection into request handling (e.g., @Req.user, custom decorators like @CurrentUser)
- Applies basic HTTP security measures: CORS configuration, Helmet, rate limiting, and secure cookies where applicable
- Understands and mitigates common web vulnerabilities (XSS, CSRF, injection, insecure direct object references) at the framework and application levels
- Ensures secure password handling (hashing, salting, password reset flows) using established libraries integrated as providers
- Protects sensitive endpoints and admin functionality via stricter authentication and authorization mechanisms
- Takes care of secure token storage, rotation strategies, and revocation where relevant
- Uses HTTPS/TLS-aware configurations and proxy headers support when running behind load balancers or API gateways","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Interceptors, Pipes, Guards, Filters & Middleware (Cross-Cutting Concerns)","scope_included":"- Understands the purpose and lifecycle of pipes, guards, interceptors, filters, and middleware and chooses the right tool for each cross-cutting concern
- Implements custom pipes for data transformation and validation beyond what DTO-based validation covers
- Implements custom guards for authentication/authorization, feature flags, or request preconditions
- Implements interceptors for logging, metrics, request/response mapping, caching, and response wrapping
- Uses Nest's built-in CacheModule and cache interceptors for endpoint-level caching when appropriate
- Implements exception filters for mapping technical errors or domain errors into consistent HTTP responses
- Applies middleware for low-level request/response manipulation, logging, or third-party integration before Nest's routing
- Configures these cross-cutting components at appropriate levels: global, module, controller, or route level based on need and impact
- Composes multiple cross-cutting components without creating hard-to-follow control flows, maintaining clear responsibility boundaries","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Async Operations, Scheduling, Events & Messaging","scope_included":"- Uses async/await correctly across controllers and services, handling Promise-based operations robustly
- Integrates background job processing or queues (e.g., Bull via @nestjs/bull or similar) through Nest modules and providers
- Implements scheduled tasks using @nestjs/schedule (Cron, intervals, timeouts) for recurring jobs
- Uses Nest's event-based patterns (EventEmitterModule or custom event bus) for decoupled intra-application communication
- Understands Nest microservices package basics and can build simple message-driven services using TCP, Redis, RMQ, NATS, Kafka, or similar transports
- Implements request-response and event-based messaging patterns using message patterns and event patterns
- Handles retries, timeouts, and error handling in messaging workflows where applicable
- Coordinates between HTTP-facing modules and background or microservice components cleanly (e.g., command side vs worker side)
- Ensures idempotency and consistency across async operations where required by business logic","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"API Design: REST, GraphQL & WebSockets","scope_included":"- Designs REST APIs with clear resource modeling, status codes, and error contracts aligned with product needs
- Documents REST APIs using @nestjs/swagger (OpenAPI) or similar, including DTOs, parameters, responses, and security schemes
- Uses NestJS GraphQL module (code-first or schema-first) to build basic to moderately complex GraphQL APIs when required
- Defines resolvers, types, inputs, and mutations and integrates them with Nest DI and service layer
- Implements GraphQL concerns such as batching, N+1 mitigation (e.g., using DataLoader), and simple authorization directives
- Uses Nest's WebSocketGateway and related decorators to implement real-time features when needed
- Manages socket connections, rooms/channels, and event flows with awareness of authentication and authorization over WebSockets
- Chooses between REST, GraphQL, and WebSockets based on requirements and can combine them within the same Nest application coherently
- Applies versioning, deprecation, and evolution strategies for APIs (REST or GraphQL) to support backward compatibility","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Testing (Unit, Integration, E2E)","scope_included":"- Uses Nest's testing utilities and Jest to write meaningful unit tests for services, controllers, and guards/pipes/interceptors
- Sets up TestingModule for unit tests with appropriate mocking of dependencies (using Jest mocks, custom providers, or testing doubles)
- Writes integration tests that involve multiple modules and actual data stores (or realistic substitutes) where needed
- Uses Supertest with Nest's testing utilities to create end-to-end tests for HTTP APIs
- Designs tests around observable behaviors rather than implementation details, maintaining test resilience to refactors
- Manages test configuration (test-specific env, in-memory DBs, or separate databases) and ensures tests are isolated and repeatable
- Uses coverage metrics to identify untested critical paths while understanding that 100% coverage is not the sole goal
- Tests error handling, edge cases, and security-sensitive behaviors (authorization, input validation) in addition to happy paths
- Organizes tests in a structure parallel to the application modules and features for maintainability
- Incorporates testing into regular development workflow (pre-commit checks, CI pipelines, pull request requirements)","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Performance, Caching, Logging & Observability","scope_included":"- Uses Nest's Logger and logger injection to produce structured, contextual logs across modules
- Configures logger levels based on environments and avoids excessive noisy logging in production
- Integrates third-party logging libraries (e.g., Pino, Winston) via custom logger services or existing Nest integrations when required
- Identifies performance bottlenecks (slow queries, N+1 issues, heavy serialization) from application logs or profiling tools
- Uses Nest's CacheModule for method-level or route-level caching and understands cache invalidation strategies
- Applies compression, GZIP, and appropriate response optimizations at framework or reverse-proxy level
- Implements basic health checks and readiness checks for the application (potentially using @nestjs/terminus)
- Integrates metrics and tracing solutions (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, APMs) via Nest modules or custom providers at a basic to intermediate level
- Designs logs and metrics to support effective debugging and incident investigation without exposing sensitive information
- Monitors resource usage patterns (memory, CPU, event loop lag) in collaboration with operations teams or infrastructure tooling","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Tooling, Local Setup & Developer Experience","scope_included":"- Uses Nest CLI effectively for scaffolding, building, testing, and running applications in different modes
- Configures TypeScript (tsconfig) for Nest projects, including path aliases, strictness, and module resolution suitable for the stack
- Uses linting and formatting tools (ESLint, Prettier) in conjunction with Nest defaults and project coding standards
- Sets up local development environments with Docker or local services (DBs, message brokers, caches) as needed by the Nest app
- Configures nodemon or similar tools for live reload during development via Nest CLI or custom scripts
- Manages environment variables locally using .env files, dotenv-safe or similar, and keeps them out of source control (except templates)
- Understands build outputs (dist folder) and how they relate to the original TypeScript sources
- Uses debugging tools (VS Code or IDE debuggers) with source maps to debug Nest applications locally
- Automates common developer tasks through NPM/Yarn scripts (lint, test, coverage, format, migration commands)
- Integrates local mock servers or stubs for external dependencies to enable offline development when practical","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Deployment, CI/CD & Runtime Operations","scope_included":"- Packages Nest applications for deployment using Node runtimes, containers (Docker), or serverless platforms as required
- Configures production builds with appropriate Node versions, environment variables, and minimal runtime dependencies
- Understands how Nest applications run behind reverse proxies or API gateways and configures trust proxy and headers correctly
- Works with process managers (PM2, systemd, container orchestrators like Kubernetes) to ensure graceful startup and shutdown
- Implements graceful shutdown in Nest (listening to shutdown signals, closing connections) using lifecycle hooks
- Collaborates with DevOps/infra teams to define health checks, probes, and monitoring endpoints
- Contributes to CI/CD pipelines for Nest projects (build, test, lint, packaging, deployment steps)
- Manages configuration and secrets via environment variables, secret managers, or configuration services across environments
- Performs basic operational troubleshooting of Nest services in production using logs, metrics, and traces
- Understands blue-green or rolling deployment implications on long-lived connections (WebSockets) and stateful components","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Collaboration, Code Quality & Documentation in NestJS Projects","scope_included":"- Participates in designing and reviewing Nest module and API architectures within a team, giving and receiving constructive feedback
- Enforces and follows coding standards and patterns specific to the team’s NestJS stack (folder structure, naming, layering)
- Writes clear inline comments and higher-level documentation where design or behavior is non-obvious
- Maintains API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL schema docs) and ensures it stays in sync with implementation
- Contributes to or maintains a project README, architecture overviews, and module-level documentation in a way newcomers can understand
- Reviews pull requests with attention to Nest-specific concerns (module boundaries, DI usage, error handling, security)
- Mentors junior developers in Nest fundamentals and common patterns through pairing and informal training
- Breaks down features into smaller tasks aligned with Nest modules and responsibilities
- Coordinates with frontend, mobile, or other service teams to align contracts and integration patterns
- Uses issue trackers and agile tools to plan, track, and communicate Nest-related work and technical debt items","is_non_core_section":true}]}
